subject: Regional routing & data placement: EU primary, APAC warm-standby constraints
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acmehealth.co.uk>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-14T09:23:00Z
Subject: Regional routing & data placement: quick Qs before SOC2 submission

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for walking us through Acme's residency constraints earlier. Before we finalize the architecture diagram for your SOC2 package I wanted to confirm a few points so our VPC/private-deploy proposal is aligned with your legal guidance:

- Production customer data (PII) must remain in the EU region at all times — no unencrypted full copies leaving the EU for any reason.
- We discussed a warm-standby in APAC; can you confirm whether encrypted backups or replicated KV-cache snapshots can be stored outside the EU under customer-managed KMS keys?
- Required RTO/RPO targets for the standby scenario (for example, RTO <= 4h, RPO <= 1h) — what should we design to satisfy your incident SLA?
- Audit log retention and access: who needs read access to audit logs (Acme SOC, Redwood ops, auditors) and are there any restrictions on where those logs are stored?

I'm attaching an initial-data-placement-diagram.png and a short residency-qa.docx that captures the legal notes you shared. Once we confirm the above we'll produce a narrow checklist for the SOC2 submission and a tabletop runbook.

Proposed next step: internal design review Wednesday (2026-04-16) and a tabletop with your security team the week after.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acmehealth.co.uk>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@acmehealth.co.uk>
Date: 2026-04-14T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Regional routing & data placement: quick Qs before SOC2 submission

Hi Marcus — thanks for the summary and for putting the diagram together. Quick clarifications from Legal/InfoSec: 

- Confirmed: Production PII must remain physically within EU-hosted infrastructure. No plaintext or unencrypted full backups may transit or be stored outside EU.
- Encrypted backups: Allowed in APAC only if (1) they are encrypted with customer-managed keys where the key material does not leave EU KMS/HSM jurisdiction, or (2) the customer maintains on-prem HSM for key escrow. We prefer option (1) but can discuss.
- Warm-standby: Acceptable as metadata-only in APAC (service routing metadata, health probes). Full KV-store or model weights cannot be resident outside EU unless encrypted and under an EU key-handling policy.
- RTO/RPO: Target RTO 4 hours, RPO 30 minutes for critical endpoints; non-critical can be 24h/6h.
- Audit logs: Acme SOC needs read access; logs must be retained in EU for 7 years, with export only via DPA-approved procedures.

We'll loop in our cloud architect (Thomas) if you need details on KMS placement. Appreciate the tabletop — propose 2026-04-23 for the run.

Sophie
Sophie Martin
Head of InfoSec, Acme Health Systems
sophie.martin@acmehealth.co.uk

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-15T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Regional routing & data placement: quick Qs before SOC2 submission

Marcus / Soojin — following Sophie's constraints I sketched a conservative deploy pattern and some controls; attaching proposed-architecture.yaml. Key points: 

- EU primary VPC: all production inference nodes, model weights, and persistent KV stores live in the EU VPC. No outbound peering to non-EU regions for storage buckets that contain PII.
- Control plane connectivity: Red/Private control plane endpoints will be reachable from the EU VPC via regional peering (Redwood-managed proxies). Control channel egress is limited to controlplane.eu.redwood.ai IP block only (deny-all, allow-listed).
- Warm-standby in APAC: run read-only, metadata-only replicas (service discovery, health, routing tables). Full state snapshots sent to APAC must be encrypted with Acme-managed EU KMS (we will support envelope encryption; Redwood never gets unencrypted keys).
- Backups: periodic encrypted backups can be stored in APAC object storage only if the envelope key is in an EU KMS with key-rotation policies and export restrictions set.
- Failover process: can trigger failover to APAC warm-standby with human approval and audited runbook trace. Failover will only instantiate full state after confirm-of-key-policy.

Outstanding asks for tabletop prep: 
1) Acme to confirm KMS key residency (EU HSM/KMS) and whether Redwood will be a key-encrypting-key (KEK) holder or not.
2) Acme sign-off on RTO/RPO above or provide changes.
3) Confirm whether auditors need direct log access or periodic exports (we prefer periodic export to minimize cross-jurisdiction access).

If agreed, I'll produce the exact ACLs and egress ACL snippets and a short playbook for the tabletop.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed-architecture.yaml (yaml)

From: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@acmehealth.co.uk>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-16T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Regional routing & data placement: quick Qs before SOC2 submission

Hi all — Thomas here (cloud architecture at Acme). A couple quick notes from our infra team: 

- We can provide an EU-based KMS (managed) with CMK residency and will not allow key export. Envelope keys for offsite backups are acceptable if the CMK remains in EU.
- Auditors: prefer periodic read-only exports to our secure auditor bucket (EU-only) rather than granting direct read access to third parties.
- Tabletop scheduling: 2026-04-23 works for the run; proposed attendees include our SOC lead and one network engineer. Expect ~90 minutes.

One ask: can Redwood provide a sanitized audit-snapshot (redacted PII) as part of the test so our auditors can validate the trace without accessing live PII?

Thanks,
Thomas
Thomas Lee
Cloud Architect, Acme Health Systems
thomas.lee@acmehealth.co.uk
